tools.name: schemathesis
tools.note: not run against the GraphQL endpoint in this example

headline.summary: 2 contract violations found in 13 requests over both query fields: a non-null field returned as null, and a valid filter that fails. The served schema also has a field (Clinician.internalNotes) that schema.graphql lacks.

findings.title: Clinician 3 resolves specialty to null although the schema says Specialty!

exchanges.request_summary: POST /graphql {"query": "{ clinicians { id name specialty rooms } }"}
POST /graphql {"query": "{ clinicians { id name specialty rooms } }"} (re-send)
POST /graphql {"query": "{ clinician(id: \"3\") { id name specialty rooms } }"}
POST /graphql {"query": "{ clinician(id: \"3\") { id name specialty rooms } }"} (re-send)

findings.expected: specialty is non-null (Specialty!), so every Clinician returned has one of GP, PHYSIO or DENTAL.
findings.actual: clinicians and clinician(id: "3") both return specialty: null for clinician 3, with no error. A GraphQL server should have nulled the parent and raised an error; this one returned invalid data.
findings.remediation: The same data defect as the REST API's missing specialty: fix the record or the resolver. If specialty can be absent, make the field nullable in schema.graphql.
findings.verification_step: Rerun send_cases.py on run-graphql with seed 1611: Query.clinicians-001 and Query.clinician-003 pass.
findings.regression_test_sketch:
def test_query_clinicians_graphql_errors(api):
    """graphql_errors: .specialty: null for non-null Specialty!"""
    resp = api.request('POST', '/graphql', json={"query": "{ clinicians { id name specialty rooms } }"})
    assert not contract_errors(resp)  # validate the body against the response schema

findings.title: clinicians(specialty: DENTAL) fails with an internal error
findings.cause: a valid query returned errors: Internal error

exchanges.request_summary: POST /graphql {"query": "{ clinicians(specialty: DENTAL) { id name specialty rooms }
POST /graphql {"query": "{ clinicians(specialty: DENTAL) { id name specialty rooms } (re-send)

findings.expected: A valid query returns data and no errors; with no dental clinicians, an empty list.
findings.remediation: Find why the DENTAL filter raises in the resolver and return an empty list when nothing matches.
findings.verification_step: Rerun with seed 1611: Query.clinicians-004 passes graphql_errors.
findings.regression_test_sketch:
def test_query_clinicians_graphql_errors(api):
    """graphql_errors: a valid query returned errors: Internal error"""
    resp = api.request('POST', '/graphql', json={"query": "{ clinicians(specialty: DENTAL) { id name specialty rooms } }"})
    assert not contract_errors(resp)  # validate the body against the response schema

contract_issues.message: the API serves Clinician.internalNotes, which isn't in the SDL

limitations: Only queries were tested; the schema has no mutations.
Argument values come from a small fixed set per scalar (IDs 1, 2, 3 and 999) and every enum value; the selection is every scalar field one level deep.
Schemathesis was not run against the GraphQL endpoint.
next_steps: Fix F1 together with the REST report's F2 (same data).
Decide whether internalNotes should be served (C1); if not, remove it from the server, otherwise add it to the SDL.
